applicant_utility.summary: ISRF is a short 3-6 month research visit funded by DST and administered by INSA, paying Rs 50,000 a month with accommodation and host-institute medical facilities included, plus one-off contingency grants of Rs 10,000 (to you) and Rs 20,000 (to your host), economy round-trip airfare and visa-fee reimbursement. The call opens once a year, normally in late December and closing at the end of March, and must be routed through the implementing agency in your country or straight to INSA where none exists. Because only the visit is funded rather than enrolment in a degree, budget for salary continuation, insurance and personal costs, and secure the Indian host supervisor's acceptance letter before you apply.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career researchers in permanent positions in the eight eligible countries with a concrete 3-6 month project and an Indian collaborator ready to host them.
application_readiness_checklist: Approach a potential Indian host supervisor early and obtain a formal acceptance letter on institute letterhead
Download the current ISRF application form and brochure from the INSA call page or dst.gov.in as soon as the call opens
Get the endorsement of your home institution's head signed before the deadline
Prepare a passport scan showing number, photo, DOB, issue and expiry dates and residential address
Assemble reprints of two recent refereed-journal publications and an up-to-date CV
Keep the sent-copy confirmation of the email to isrf.dst@insa.nic.in
common_rejection_risks: Applying without a Letter of Acceptance from an Indian host supervisor
Late submission - the brochure states no application beyond the deadline will be accepted
Missing endorsement from the head of the home institution
Age cut-off is fixed to the stated date (below 45 as on 31 March 2026), not your birthday in the application year
Holding any Indian temporary or permanent residency visa, which disqualifies outright
A generic research write-up with no fit to the proposed host lab
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Salary forgone during the visit, personal/travel insurance, daily living costs beyond the Rs 50,000 monthly allowance, and any costs of accompanying family.

applicant_utility.summary: This UGC scheme funds students and teachers from developing countries in Asia, Africa and Latin America to pursue M.Phil./Ph.D. (JRF) or postdoctoral (RA) research at an Indian university, with a published monthly fellowship (Rs 18,600 as JRF, Rs 21,700 as SRF, Rs 25,000 as RA, with HRA and contingency additional) plus annual contingency. There is no online portal and no fixed deadline: applications are circulated through Indian embassies and missions, endorsed locally, then screened by UGC committees for only about 20 JRF and 7 RA slots a year. Foreign nationals already in India apply through the university they want to work with instead, so the embassy is not the only door if you are already resident.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Master's or doctorate holders from developing countries outside India seeking funded research registration at an Indian university who are comfortable working through diplomatic channels.
application_readiness_checklist: Ask the Indian embassy or mission in your country whether the current-year circulation for this scheme is open
Line up a willing Indian university supervisor and department before preparing the file
Ensure the endorsement of the Indian embassy or mission is stamped on the application form itself
Prepare the required copies of the form and enclosures (academic records, DOB evidence, photographs, ~500-word research plan)
Check the age limit as on 1 July of the application year before investing in the paperwork
common_rejection_risks: Mission-level screening happens before UGC ever sees the file, so a locally weak application fails there
Only 20 JRF and 7 RA slots exist nationally, making this one of the smallest UGC fellowship windows
Missing embassy endorsement makes the application inadmissible for Commission consideration
Age cut-off is applied to 1 July of the application year, not the joining date
The fellowship can be terminated mid-tenure by the Commission, and its decision is final
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition and institutional fees of the host university, living costs beyond the fellowship and any HRA or hostel entitlement, and travel to India - no airfare or relocation allowance is published.
document_audit: Certified copies of academic records must match the form copies exactly
A certified date-of-birth document is required; a passport copy alone is not listed
Photographs must be stapled one per form copy where multiple copies are submitted
The research plan statement and its abstract each have a 500-word ceiling
The embassy endorsement must appear on the application form itself, not on a separate letter, where the form requires it
alerts: No fixed deadline means timing is controlled locally by each mission - enquire directly and early
UGC publishes differing rates across its own plan-period documents and later brochures; confirm the rate in force before budgeting
The Research Associateship is initially two years and extendable by two - it is not guaranteed for four
UGC can withdraw or terminate the award, and the rules treat the Commission's decision as final
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the endorsed application to your Indian embassy or mission (or via your Indian host university if already in India); local screening forwards the file to UGC's Selection and Award Bureau for committee consideration.
